plan: In a single-round sealed bid auction with rational opponents, the optimal strategy is to bid strategically near my private value. Since my value is $31, I want to win without overpaying. I'll bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. Rational opponents will also bid strategically. I'll choose a bid that balances winning probability with profit margin - around $28-$30 seems optimal to create a buffer against overpaying while still having a strong chance of winning.

With a private value of $37, I want to win the auction but minimize my payment. Other rational bidders will likely bid strategically based on their own values. I'll aim to bid slightly above the expected second-highest bid. Given the uniform distribution of values, a bid around $35-$38 seems optimal to maximize potential profit while having a good chance of winning.

With a private value of $11, I want to bid strategically. Since this is a single round, I'll aim to win only if my bid doesn't exceed my value. Other bidders are rational and will also try to maximize profit. A dominant strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to create a buffer. I'll bid $10.9 - this leaves me a small profit margin if I win, and protects against overpaying.
